assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of political-economy research connecting political institutions, state capacity, accountability and fiscal choices to economic development and distribution.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are central, distinct contributors to the modern theoretical and empirical political-economy framework.
assessment.maturity: The research program has shaped several decades of work and has broad relevance across comparative institutions and public finance.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several connected programs, making a sharply bounded citation and complete attribution difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and made local, institutional and policy correlates of opportunity empirically tractable.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are principal architects of the linked-data mobility research program.
assessment.maturity: The methods and findings have generated a large literature and an enduring public-finance research infrastructure.
uncertainties: The evidence is especially rooted in particular administrative-data settings, and causal interpretation of geographic patterns remains challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction of long-run income and wealth inequality, including hidden wealth, has substantially changed empirical research and policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman are leading and complementary contributors to the data, measurement and interpretation of top incomes and wealth.
assessment.maturity: The work has accumulated over decades and is widely used as a benchmark for distributional analysis.
uncertainties: Coverage, capitalization and offshore-wealth measurement involve consequential assumptions.
The appropriate division of credit across a large collaborative data enterprise is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression provided a durable general framework for studying distributional heterogeneity rather than only conditional means.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett introduced the core method and are its unambiguous central originators.
assessment.maturity: The approach is long established, broadly adopted across economics and statistics, and continues to support substantive research.
uncertainties: Its fundamental importance is methodological, so comparison with more directly substantive discoveries requires judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how economists formulate credible conclusions when assumptions cannot justify point identification.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the defining intellectual source of the program; later contributions extend its application and inference.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been influential for decades in econometrics, treatment-effect analysis and policy evaluation.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping combines a broad foundational program with later technical developments whose relative credit is less clear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work supplied major economic foundations for valuing exhaustible natural capital, biodiversity and sustainability across generations.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal jointly established central theoretical building blocks for this research agenda.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is mature and increasingly consequential as environmental constraints enter economic accounting and policy.
uncertainties: The bridge from theoretical valuation to operational biodiversity measurement remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion supplied influential alternatives to narrowly self-interested models and reshaped experimental and labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Fehr, Falk and Schmidt made prominent complementary theoretical and experimental contributions to social-preferences research.
assessment.maturity: The literature is extensive and its mechanisms have been tested in many economic settings.
uncertainties: The breadth of related behavioural contributors makes exclusive attribution difficult.
The stability and external validity of measured preferences vary across contexts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony has changed the understanding of wage setting, employer power and the incidence of labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied a central modern framework, while Naidu has been an important contributor to its empirical and institutional development.
assessment.maturity: The subject has become a major and policy-relevant labour-economics program with growing empirical support.
uncertainties: The evidence for the magnitude and sources of monopsony power is heterogeneous across labour markets.
The field is still rapidly developing, and the allocation of credit remains unsettled.
